action: The PIPC advises checking that the sender's address matches the agency's official domain, not opening suspicious attachments or links, not installing remote-control apps, and reporting such emails to the police or the Personal Information Infringement Reporting Center.
date_note: Fnnews's article of 24 November reports the warning issued that day; the page gives no earlier day for when the emails began.
exec: Malicious emails posing as staff of South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission claim a data leak occurred, the commission warns.
geo_basis: country as stated; the agency's city is not given in the source
plain: Fake emails pretending to come from South Korea's data protection commission say your personal data leaked and push you to click a link or open an attachment. The commission warns about them.
summary: Fnnews reports that South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission has warned of malicious emails impersonating its staff and claiming a personal data leak occurred. The emails push recipients to click a link or open an attachment, with the aim, per the commission, of stealing account and financial credentials or installing malware. Attachments carry titles such as a guide or a compensation application.
title: South Korea's data protection commission warns of malicious emails impersonating its staff

validation.note: Only Fnnews's report of the commission's warning was read; the commission's own notice was not found.
